A Car is composed of an Engine and four Wheels. The Engine is part of the Car and cannot exist independently.
A House consists of many Rooms. Each Room is part of exactly one House and is destroyed when the House is removed.
An Order is composed of one or more OrderItems. An OrderItem cannot exist without its parent Order.
University is composed of many Departments. A Department belongs to exactly one University.
A Document is composed of Pages. A Page is part of exactly one Document.
A Teacher can teach many Courses. A Course can have one or more Teachers. Each teaching assignment has a semester.
A Team has one or more Developers. Each Developer belongs to exactly one Team.
A Movie can have many Actors. An Actor can appear in many Movies. Each appearance has a character name.
A Student can enrol in 1 to 10 Courses per semester. A Course can have 5 to 200 Students.
A Project has one or more Teams. Each Team has exactly one TeamLead and one to fifteen Members.
An Author can write many Books. A Book can have multiple Authors. Each authorship has a contribution role.

User sends searchQuery() to Web Server. Web Server sends query() to SQL Server. SQL Server returns results() to Web Server. Web Server returns searchResults() to User.

User sends a search request to Web Server. Web Server forwards the query to SQL Server. If results are found, SQL Server returns data to Web Server and Web Server returns searchResults to User. Otherwise, Web Server returns emptyResults to User.

User sends pay() to Payment Gateway. Payment Gateway sends authorise() to Transaction Server. Transaction Server sends verifyFunds() to Bank. Bank returns fundsAvailable() to Transaction Server. Transaction Server returns authorised() to Payment Gateway. Payment Gateway returns receipt() to User.

Customer sends payment request to Payment Gateway. Payment Gateway contacts Transaction Server. Transaction Server contacts Bank. If bank approves, Bank confirms approval to Transaction Server and Transaction Server returns confirmation to Payment Gateway and Payment Gateway returns receipt to Customer. Otherwise Bank rejects to Transaction Server and Payment Gateway returns failure to Customer.

User inserts card and sends PIN to ATM. ATM sends verifyPin() to Bank. Bank confirms pin is valid. ATM requests withdrawal amount. ATM sends withdrawalRequest() to Bank. If balance is sufficient, Bank confirms approval and ATM dispenses cash. Otherwise, Bank rejects with insufficient funds.
Customer sends withdraw() to ATM. ATM sends authenticate() to Bank. Bank confirms identity() to ATM. ATM sends debit() to Bank. Bank returns debited() to ATM. ATM returns cash() to Customer.

User sends checkout() to Order Service. Order Service sends reserveStock() to Inventory Service and debitAccount() to Payment Service simultaneously. Inventory Service returns stockReserved() to Order Service. Payment Service returns paymentTaken() to Order Service. Order Service returns orderConfirmed() to User.

API Gateway sends authenticate() to Auth Service and fetchProfile() to User Service in parallel. Auth Service returns authToken() to API Gateway. User Service returns profileData() to API Gateway. API Gateway returns response() to Client.

User sends insertCoin() to Register. Register returns coinAccepted() to User. User sends selectSoda() to Register. Register sends checkStock() to Dispenser. If soda is available, Dispenser returns sodaAvailable() to Register. Register sends dispenseSoda() to Dispenser. Dispenser returns sodaDispensed() to Register. Register returns change() to User. Otherwise Dispenser returns outOfStock() to Register. Register returns refundCoin() to User.

Register sends checkAvailability() to Dispenser. If soda is available, Dispenser returns sodaReady() to Register and Register sends releaseSoda() to Dispenser. Otherwise Dispenser returns outOfStock() to Register. Register returns refundCoin() to User.
Client sends request() to Server. Server sends query() to Database. Database returns data() to Server. Server returns response() to Client.

User sends login() to AuthService. AuthService sends findUser() to UserRepository. UserRepository returns user() to AuthService. If credentials match, AuthService returns token() to User. Otherwise AuthService returns invalidCredentials() to User.

User --> WebServer : 1 searchMessage()
WebServer --> WebServer : 1.1 createSQLQuery()
WebServer --> SQLServer : 1.2 sendSQLQuery()
SQLServer --> WebServer : 1.3 queryResult()
WebServer --> User : 2 searchResults()

Collaboration diagram: User sends searchMessage() to WebServer. WebServer creates an SQL query internally. WebServer sends the query to SQLServer. SQLServer returns the result to WebServer. WebServer returns searchResults to User.

Objects: User, WebServer, SQLServer. User --> WebServer : 1 search(). WebServer --> WebServer : 1.1 buildQuery(). WebServer --> SQLServer : 1.2 executeQuery(). SQLServer --> WebServer : 1.3 rows(). WebServer --> User : 2 results().

Communication diagram for web search: User interacts with WebServer. WebServer interacts with SQLServer. Messages: 1 searchMessage() from User to WebServer, 1.1 createSQLQuery() self-call on WebServer, 1.2 sendSQLQuery() from WebServer to SQLServer, 1.3 queryResult() from SQLServer to WebServer, 2 searchResults() from WebServer to User.

Draw a collaboration diagram showing User, WebServer, and SQLServer. The user sends a search request. WebServer processes it internally and queries the SQLServer. SQLServer returns data and WebServer responds to User.

User --> WebServer : 1 initiatePayment()
WebServer --> WebServer : 1.1 validateInput()
WebServer --> SQLServer : 1.2 getUserAccount()
SQLServer --> WebServer : 1.3 accountDetails()
WebServer --> TransactionServer : 2 processPayment()
TransactionServer --> TransactionServer : 2.1 [amount > 1000] requestConfirmation()
TransactionServer --> SQLServer : 2.2 debitAccount()
SQLServer --> TransactionServer : 2.3 debitConfirmed()
TransactionServer --> WebServer : 3 paymentResult()
WebServer --> User : 4 paymentConfirmation()

Collaboration diagram for electronic payment. Participants: User, WebServer, SQLServer, TransactionServer. User sends initiatePayment() to WebServer. WebServer validates input internally. WebServer retrieves account from SQLServer. WebServer sends processPayment() to TransactionServer. If amount exceeds 1000, TransactionServer requests confirmation. TransactionServer debits account via SQLServer. TransactionServer returns paymentResult to WebServer. WebServer returns paymentConfirmation to User.

Objects: User, WebServer, TransactionServer, SQLServer. Messages: 1 pay() User to WebServer, 1.1 validateCard() WebServer self-call, 1.2 getAccount() WebServer to SQLServer, 1.3 accountData() SQLServer to WebServer, 2 authorise() WebServer to TransactionServer, 2.1 debit() TransactionServer to SQLServer, 2.2 debited() SQLServer to TransactionServer, 3 receipt() TransactionServer to WebServer, 4 confirmation() WebServer to User.

Communication diagram: User, PaymentGateway, TransactionServer, Bank. 1 pay() from User to PaymentGateway. 1.1 authorise() from PaymentGateway to TransactionServer. 1.2 verifyFunds() from TransactionServer to Bank. 1.3 [balance >= amount] fundsAvailable() from Bank to TransactionServer. 1.4 approved() from TransactionServer to PaymentGateway. 2 receipt() from PaymentGateway to User.

Draw a collaboration diagram for an electronic payment scenario with User, WebServer, SQLServer, and TransactionServer. Include numbered messages for payment initiation, account lookup, transaction processing with a conditional confirmation for high-value amounts, and a final payment confirmation.

User --> ATM : 2 enterPin()
ATM --> Bank : 2.1 verifyPin()
Bank --> ATM : 2.2 pinValid()

ATM --> CashDispenser : 3.4 dispenseCash()

Collaboration diagram for ATM withdrawal. Objects: User, ATM, Bank, CashDispenser. User inserts card and ATM verifies it with Bank. User enters PIN and ATM verifies PIN with Bank. User requests withdrawal. ATM checks daily limit internally. ATM debits account at Bank. If balance is sufficient, Bank confirms and ATM instructs CashDispenser to dispense cash. ATM returns receipt to User.

Communication diagram: User, ATM, Bank. 1 insertCard() from User to ATM. 1.1 authenticateCard() from ATM to Bank. 1.2 cardOk() from Bank to ATM. 2 enterPin() from User to ATM. 2.1 validatePin() from ATM to Bank. 2.2 pinOk() from Bank to ATM. 3 withdraw() from User to ATM. 3.1 checkBalance() from ATM to Bank. 3.2 [balance >= amount] approved() from Bank to ATM. 3.3 dispenseCash() ATM self-call. 4 returnCard() from ATM to User.

Objects: ATM, Bank, CashDispenser. ATM interacts with Bank and CashDispenser. Numbered messages: 1 verifyCard() ATM to Bank, 2 verifyPin() ATM to Bank, 3 withdrawalRequest() ATM to Bank, 3.1 checkFunds() Bank self-call, 3.2 [approved] authorise() Bank to ATM, 4 dispenseCash() ATM to CashDispenser, 5 receipt() ATM to User.

Draw a collaboration diagram for an ATM cash withdrawal involving User, ATM, Bank, and CashDispenser. Show card verification, PIN validation, balance checking with a conditional approval, cash dispensing, and receipt generation using hierarchical sequence numbers.

Register --> Dispenser : 2.3 dispenseSoda()

Register --> User : 3 deliverSoda()

Collaboration diagram for a soda vending machine. Objects: User, Register, Dispenser. User inserts coin; Register validates it internally. User selects soda; Register checks stock with Dispenser. If stock is available Dispenser confirms and Register instructs Dispenser to release soda. Register delivers soda and returns change to User.

Communication diagram: User, Register, Dispenser. 1 insertCoin() from User to Register. 1.1 checkCoin() Register self-call. 2 selectItem() from User to Register. 2.1 checkAvailability() from Register to Dispenser. 2.2 [available] itemReady() from Dispenser to Register. 2.3 releaseItem() from Register to Dispenser. 2.4 itemDispensed() from Dispenser to Register. 3 soda() from Register to User. 4 change() from Register to User.

Objects: User, Register, Dispenser. Messages with sequence numbers: 1 coinInserted() User to Register, 1.1 validateCoin() Register self-call, 2 sodaSelected() User to Register, 2.1 checkInventory() Register to Dispenser, 2.2 [count > 0] inStock() Dispenser to Register, 2.3 dispenseSoda() Register to Dispenser, 3 sodaDelivered() Register to User, 4 changeReturned() Register to User.

Draw a collaboration diagram for a soda machine scenario with User, Register, and Dispenser. Include coin insertion with internal validation, soda selection, stock checking with a conditional availability response, soda dispensing, and change return.
